items.title: Max Verstappen: “I really thought that we would not win a race this year”
items.summary: Heading into the Las Vegas Grand Prix on a run of eight consecutive podiums, Max Verstappen looks every bit the force who dominated Formula 1 earlier this decade. Back in March, however, the four-time world champion was braced for his first winless campaign since 2015.

items.title: Fernando Alonso returns to Dakar: Why his first rally-raid experience was a shock to the system
items.summary: While Fernando Alonso reiterated in Las Vegas that, in his view, Formula 1 has thrown away 16 years of pure racing before the return of V8 engines in 2030, the Spaniard continues to seek those pure challenges outside the pinnacle of motorsport as well.

items.title: How the F1 2026 regulations neutered Oscar Piastri's "real strength"
items.summary: McLaren boss Zak Brown reckons Oscar Piastri’s struggles in the 2026 Formula 1 season stem from high-speed corners being his strength - but the new cars require a different technique. F1 introduced its latest regulation overhaul this year with power units being more electrical, causing battery management to contentiously play a key role in the racing.

items.title: What Flavio Briatore takes from McLaren after Fernando Alonso "disaster"
items.summary: Disappointment, infighting, and a revolving door of senior personnel have characterised Alpine's ‘lost decade' after Renault acquired the Enstone-based team at the end of 2015. Current boss Flavio Briatore says Alpine can take some inspiration from McLaren, which claimed the constructors' championship in 2024 and '25, and helped Lando Norris to the drivers' title last year.

items.title: "It was scary at 100km/h" - F1 drivers shocked by Las Vegas 'ice rink'
items.summary: With rain affecting Thursday's Las Vegas Grand Prix running on the low-grip street circuit around the Strip, the biggest takeaway was not who was fastest, but the impressive fact that every Formula 1 driver kept it out of the barriers.

items.title: George Russell impressed by "exceptionally fast" McLaren as rain delays Lando Norris' floor test
items.summary: George Russell came out of nowhere to set the fastest time in the closing stages of the second Formula 1 practice session in Las Vegas, although Alpine driver Pierre Gasly almost caused a major surprise by beating him. The Frenchman ultimately fell just 0.071 seconds short, leaving the Mercedes works team at the top of the timesheets.

items.title: Pirelli reintroduces stint limit for F1 Qatar GP
items.summary: Formula 1 teams will again have to follow a prescribed stint limit for each car at the Qatar Grand Prix to protect the Pirelli tyres around the high-degradation track. Drivers must complete no more than 27 laps per stint at Lusail International Circuit, meaning teams will likely opt for a two-stop strategy in the 57-lap race.

items.title: "Same as Brazil" – Red Bull "trying to understand" the root cause of Max Verstappen's complaints
items.summary: After Thursday's practice sessions in Las Vegas, Red Bull – like all Formula 1 teams – has been left with very few answers. Isack Hadjar eventually finished fourth on the timesheets, but that means very little given that no more rain is forecast for the remainder of the weekend.

items.title: Lewis Hamilton plans "GTA VI" session after Vegas FP2: "I'm like a big kid"
items.summary: Lewis Hamilton finished sixth in a slippery second practice for the Las Vegas Grand Prix, before what he had promised fans would be an early night at his hotel with the newly released Grand Theft Auto VI. The seven-time world champion was speaking on stage at PUMA's Under the Lights fan event at its Las Vegas store on Tuesday night, two days before the game's release.

items.title: Lewis Hamilton launches alien-themed Area 44 collection for Las Vegas GP
items.summary: Seven-time Formula 1 champion Lewis Hamilton's fashion label +44 has returned to Las Vegas with Area 44, an alien-themed collection released ahead of this weekend's grand prix. The range is on sale through the +44 website and at a pop-up on the Encore Esplanade at Wynn Las Vegas, which runs until Sunday. The Briton showed it off to his followers on Instagram.

items.title: Isack Hadjar: "I realised why Max is a four-time world champion"
items.summary: Isack Hadjar says his first season as Max Verstappen's team-mate at Red Bull has opened his eyes to why the Dutchman is a four-time Formula 1 world champion. Hadjar moved up from Racing Bulls for his 2026 campaign, taking one of the most pressured seats in F1 alongside Verstappen.

items.title: Zak Brown explains why McLaren keeps selling F1 cars before they race ahead of 2027 auction
items.summary: McLaren Racing CEO Zak Brown has explained why the Woking outfit is selling its Formula 1 cars at auction before they have even turned a wheel, saying the alternative is leaving them hidden away. McLaren will auction its 2027 car, the MCL41, with RM Sotheby's in Abu Dhabi on 9 December, three days after the season finale.

items.title: Zak Brown says McLaren will always respect staff who want to skip Middle East races
items.summary: Formula 1 is pressing ahead with its season-ending swing through the Middle East, and McLaren is making clear that no member of its travelling workforce will be forced onto the plane.

items.title: F1 Las Vegas GP: George Russell pips Pierre Gasly in tricky FP2
items.summary: George Russell pipped Pierre Gasly to go fastest in second practice for the Formula 1 Las Vegas Grand Prix thanks to a last-gasp effort in slippery conditions. The Mercedes driver set a 1m47.272s as the chequered flag flew, putting him 0.071s ahead of Gasly, who benefitted from track evolution to take a shock second for Alpine.

items.title: Where to see F1 cars in Las Vegas without a race ticket
items.summary: You do not need a grandstand seat to get close to a Formula 1 car in Las Vegas this week. Teams, partners and resorts have parked show cars and replicas all over the Strip for the Las Vegas Grand Prix, and most of them are free to visit. Here is where to find them. Mercedes, Bellagio The world champions have the biggest set-up.

items.title: Five drivers set for grid penalties for engine changes at F1 Las Vegas GP
items.summary: Five drivers will take grid penalties for the Las Vegas Grand Prix, including new Formula 1 world champion Kimi Antonelli. As previously indicated by Mercedes, Antonelli will take a five-place grid drop for an internal combustion engine change – but does not pick up a further penalty for a turbocharger change due to still being within his allocation.

items.title: Zak Brown confirms “agreement in principle” on F1’s V8 return after deleted FIA posts
items.summary: Confusion hung over the Las Vegas Grand Prix paddock all week after official FIA social media channels briefly published—and abruptly deleted—graphics declaring an agreement in principle to bring V8 engines back to Formula 1 in 2030.

items.title: Cadillac scraps V6 F1 engine, delays entry as PU manufacturer
items.summary: Cadillac is set to delay the introduction of its in-house Formula 1 power unit by a year to 2030. The American squad's initial plan was to compete in the championship with its own General Motors power unit for the first time in 2029.

items.title: F1 Las Vegas GP: Rain ruins FP1 running
items.summary: "If we're on a track like Vegas and it rains, honestly, I think we're in trouble," Racing Bulls driver Liam Lawson predicted after sampling this year's rain tyres in Brazil.

items.title: Lando Norris confident F1 would not "put us at risk" in the Middle East
items.summary: 2025 Formula 1 champion Lando Norris says he has no concerns about the final two races of the season in the Middle East, insisting the championship would not put its drivers and teams at risk. After this weekend's race in Las Vegas, the championship heads to Qatar from 27-29 November and then Abu Dhabi from 4-6 December.

items.title: Nike joins F1 as apparel partner
items.summary: Athletic apparel giant Nike has joined F1 as its official partner and uniform supplier, taking over from Puma at the start of 2027. As was long rumoured, Nike will start supplying F1 personnel with apparel and footwear form the start of next season, a partnership that also extends to F1 Academy, which had both been using Puma kit until this year.

items.title: Lewis Hamilton backs V8 return, hits out at 2026 engines “dying” on straights
items.summary: Lewis Hamilton has raced through every season of Formula 1's V6 turbo-hybrid era, and he is not shy about what the latest rules are getting wrong. Speaking on Las Vegas Grand Prix media day, the seven-time world champion welcomed the FIA's push to bring back V8 engines - while taking a blunt jab at how the current 2026 power units fade down the straights.

items.title: Oscar Piastri addresses management plans after Mark Webber split
items.summary: McLaren Formula 1 driver Oscar Piastri says his upcoming management structure is yet to be defined, after his partnership with managers Ann and Mark Webber was terminated. Piastri put out a joint press release on 9 November, indicating he and the Webbers had “mutually ended their agreement”.

items.title: Lewis Hamilton opens up on "isolating" feeling after seeing his own F1 Las Vegas grandstand
items.summary: Nearly two decades into his Formula 1 career, Lewis Hamilton still is not taking the scale of his following for granted. Speaking on media day ahead of the 2026 Las Vegas Grand Prix, the seven-time world champion offered a rare glimpse into the emotional toll of paddock life when asked what it meant to see fans packing his own dedicated grandstand at the circuit.

items.title: Lando Norris: “A hell of a lot of money” riding on McLaren’s fight for third
items.summary: With Mercedes having already sealed the 2026 constructors' championship and Ferrari sitting clear in second, McLaren's remaining focus across Las Vegas, Qatar, and Abu Dhabi comes down to one battle: overturning a 17-point deficit to Red Bull Racing for third place. Red Bull enters the Las Vegas Grand Prix on 415 points to McLaren's 398.

items.title: Lewis Hamilton addresses speculation around Ferrari "trust" issues
items.summary: Lewis Hamilton has insisted there are zero “trust” problems at Ferrari despite him overruling strategic calls becoming a repeated occurrence across recent Formula 1 grands prix. The seven-time world champion has ignored calls to pit in two of the last four rounds - Singapore and Brazil - with both backfiring on the Scuderia driver.

items.title: Charles Leclerc on journalist ban: “I was surprised by the choice of words”
items.summary: Charles Leclerc had no hand in getting a veteran Formula 1 reporter barred from the paddock, and he isn't interested in policing the press - even when the headlines get a little personal.

items.title: Rafael Camara torn between his F2 title bid and more F1 races with Haas
items.summary: Rafael Camara is torn between completing his title-contending Formula 2 campaign and seeing out the 2026 season at Haas in Formula 1. The Ferrari protege is the reigning F3 champion and leads the F2 standings as a rookie with Invicta Racing, courtesy of a starring campaign in which he has taken five pole positions and seven feature race podiums including three victories.

items.title: Lewis Hamilton: "You can't be the only one pushing for change" in F1
items.summary: Lewis Hamilton says he had hoped others in Formula 1 would follow his lead in speaking out on issues around the world, but admitted that "so far that's not the case". The seven-time world champion has used his platform for causes including diversity in motorsport and, more recently, the humanitarian crisis in Gaza.

items.title: Honda reveals key F1 power unit change for 2027
items.summary: Immediately after the Sao Paulo Grand Prix, Honda was still unable to fully explain Lance Stroll's DNF. The Canadian was forced to retire for the 14th time, equalling the all-time record for the most retirements in a single Formula 1 season.
